fullText:
Summary: Access Engineering PLC (AEL.N0000) has grown into a construction, vehicle, property and condominium group, and profits are rising fast: the first quarter of this year was up 78%. But at Rs 77.20 the share trades at 1.8x its NAV of Rs 41.95 and 13.2x earnings once a one-off property revaluation gain is taken out. Much of the near-term profit is the one-time sale of flats at Marina Square, and the group's normal return on equity is only about 13%, below what a Sri Lankan investor should demand. Counting the Marina Square profit still to come, the methods put fair value at about Rs 47, so the price is about 64% above it. I'd buy at up to about Rs 40 and treat under Rs 35 as a strong buy.

Price and key figures
Price: Rs 77.20 (Interim report to 30 Jun 2026 (quarter-end price), 2026-06-30). Please check it live. In April–June 2026 it traded between Rs 66.90 and Rs 79.50. It closed the year to March 2026 at Rs 67.00, up from Rs 38.50 a year earlier; that year's high was Rs 80.50 (February 2026) and low Rs 34.80 (April 2025).
Three months to 30 June 2026 (group, unaudited): revenue more than doubled to Rs 16.6bn and profit attributable rose 78% to Rs 1.71bn. EPS was Rs 1.71 against Rs 0.96. NAV per share was Rs 41.95.
What drove it: Marina Square flat handovers brought Rs 2.57bn of revenue and Rs 0.79bn of profit (nothing a year earlier), and vehicle sales (Sathosa Motors and Access Motors) rose to Rs 8.06bn from Rs 2.26bn. Construction profit fell, and finance costs nearly tripled to Rs 1.40bn as borrowing rose.
Year to March 2026 (group, audited): revenue Rs 49.7bn (up 44%), profit attributable Rs 7.17bn, EPS Rs 7.17 (Rs 6.31), reported ROE 18%, dividends Rs 2.00.
One-off: that year includes a Rs 4.01bn gain from revaluing investment property (mainly the Ekala logistics park), less about Rs 1.96bn of deferred tax on it. Without it, profit attributable was about Rs 5.12bn, or Rs 5.12 a share, an ROE of about 12.6%.
Debt: borrowings Rs 43.9bn and net debt about Rs 38.8bn at June 2026, about 0.9x equity (debt to equity 99%). Interest cover fell to about 4x.
History: EPS was Rs 5.11 (2021/22), Rs 2.48 (2022/23), Rs 6.86 (2023/24, helped by a Rs 2.55bn tax credit and a Rs 1.11bn revaluation gain), Rs 6.31 (2024/25) and Rs 7.17 (2025/26).

Methods
NAV (Rs 41.95): 1.8x. About Rs 40.8bn of the book is investment property at valuers' prices, and Rs 34.4bn is Marina Square flats held at cost.
Return on equity: 18% reported for 2025/26, about 12.6% without the revaluation gain. It was 7.6% in 2022/23 and 14.7% in 2024/25.
P/E: 9.7x trailing reported EPS of Rs 7.92, but 13.2x trailing EPS of Rs 5.87 without the revaluation gain. Year-end P/E: 9.3x (2026), 6.1x (2025).
Dividends: Rs 2.00 a year for the last two years (two Rs 1.00 interim dividends), a 2.6% yield; about 39% of profit without the revaluation gain.
Marina Square: the flats still on the books cost Rs 34.4bn (March 2026), and customers had paid about Rs 20.2bn in advances. In the first quarter the flats handed over earned a 34% operating margin. I count the profit still to come as extra value of Rs 2.8 / 7.7 / 10.4 a share (after tax, discounted for the time it takes to sell and hand over).
Adjusted NAV (NAV plus Marina Square profit, times 0.85 / 1.0 / 1.1): Rs 38.0 / 49.7 / 57.6, weighted Rs 47.8.
P/E method (EPS without Marina Square or revaluation gains, plus Marina Square value): Rs 38.8 / 62.7 / 88.4, weighted Rs 60.7.
Residual income (plus Marina Square value): Rs 20.3 / 34.1 / 53.2, weighted Rs 33.8.
Dividend model: Rs 15.4 / 21.5 / 36.5 (not used in the fair value).

AEL pays out well under half its profit, so a dividend model understates it. Its cash flow is dominated by Marina Square and vehicle stock, so a cash-flow DCF isn't reliable. Price to book is folded into the adjusted-NAV method. Residual income is the strictest because the group's normal ROE is below the cost of equity; the P/E method is the most generous.

Assumptions (bear / base / bull)
Cost of equity: 18% / 16.5% / 15%.
Normal ROE (residual income): 12% falling to 11% / 13.5% falling to 13% / 15.5% falling to 15%.
Long-term growth: 5% / 6% / 7%.
EPS for the year to March 2027 without Marina Square × P/E: 4.5 × 8 / 5.5 × 10 / 6.5 × 12.
Marina Square margin on the remaining flats: 15% / 30% / 35% before tax, sold over about three years.
Average of the three methods: Rs 32.4 / Rs 48.8 / Rs 66.4.
Common: Sri Lankan 7–10-year government bonds yield about 12% (October 2026). Tax 30%. Revaluation gains are left out of earnings because they don't produce cash. Payout 35%.

Fair value and buy price
Fair value: weighting 30/50/20 gives about Rs 47 (1.1x NAV), so Rs 77.20 is about 64% above it.
Buy price: a 15% margin of safety gives Rs 40.00, and 25% gives Rs 35.30.
Plan for 500 shares: 200 at up to Rs 47.00, 150 at up to Rs 40.00 and 150 at up to Rs 35.30. That averages about Rs 41.39, about Rs 20,695, against Rs 38,600 at Rs 77.20.
Realism: Rs 47 needs about a 39% fall. The share hasn't been below Rs 66.90 since the start of April 2026 and was last under Rs 47 in mid-2025, so these prices probably need a broad market fall or a disappointment on Marina Square sales.

Sensitivity (residual income base case plus Marina Square, Rs per share)
Cost of equity 15%: 30.2 / 39.4 / 56.7 for normal ROE of 11% / 13% / 16%.
Cost of equity 16.5%: 26.6 / 34.1 / 47.8.
Cost of equity 18%: 24.0 / 30.1 / 41.3.
Today's price needs ROE of well over 16% for many years, or a much larger Marina Square profit.

What would change my view
Supports a higher value: Marina Square flats selling quickly at good margins; commercial space there leased well; new government infrastructure contracts lifting construction profit; vehicle sales staying strong; debt falling as Marina Square cash comes in; a higher dividend.
Supports a lower value: unsold Marina Square flats or price cuts; vehicle import rules tightening again; finance costs rising further; more profit coming from revaluation gains rather than cash earnings; slow government payments for construction work.

These are my estimates from the annual reports for the years to March 2025 and March 2026 and the interim reports to June 2026. The interim figures are unaudited, so check the price before ordering. This is analysis, not personal financial advice.
